newsitem.title: UK: DHL UK sees 15 pct pa growth for nxt 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: DHL UK sees 15 pct pa growth for nxt 5 yrs.

text.p: DHL International(UK) Ltd anticipates volume growth of around 15 percent annually for the next four to five years, managing director Nick Butcher told a news conference on Wednesday.

Commercial director Glyn Jones added: "Anticipated revenue in 1996 will exceed our own very ambitious expectations...and this growth is in excess of 20 percent compared with 1995," but did not give any precise figures.
However DHL UK now expects to exceed 300 million sterling in turnover in 1998, two years ahead of the previous target date of 2000, Jones said.
"And this is largely due to our performance in 1996 with long-haul parcels making an important contribution. There was also a 36 percent rise in parcels to European Union countries."
"October saw daily turnover exceeding one million sterling for the first time," Jones added.
Butcher said: "Although the UK market is more mature than the Asia-Pacific or East European markets...we are pretty optimistic about the outlook."
The growth would reflect an expanding market,as well as "our product differentation from the competition and gains from the air freight forwarding sector," he added.
Replying to questions, Jones said he estimated that over the past five years DHL had gained three percentage points of the total airfreight market from forwarders.
He said the trend towards greater use of integrators -- instead of forwarders -- by exporters and importers for air shipments was likely to accelerate.
Jones added that the average weight of packages carried by DHL was around 15 kg, with unconsolidated cargo handled by forwarders around 30 kg.
He cited a U.S. study which showed that most new airfreight exports from the U.S. "are now being moved by integrators rather than traditional forwarders."

Butcher added: "Overall the future for integrators is pretty bright," referringto forecasts made earlier this year by the Boeing Co that the express market would grow by 18 percent annually for the next 20 years.
